text:
sam: heads-up — noticed a big burst of failed scrapes from gke-west2 auth-proxy, prometheus p95 scrape latency jumped to ~15s, remote_write backlog increasing :rotating_light:

marta: ugh, saw the Grafana panel too. a bunch of 401/502s from the auth service in the auth-proxy logs. any recent config changes on the proxy?

raj: not deployed anything for auth-proxy in the last 24h. but we did roll a k8s nodepool scaling yesterday that changed source IP ranges. could be mTLS/token audience mismatch.

infra-bot: alert: prometheus.remote_write.backlog > 5000 (gke-west2-prometheus-1) — triggered at 2026-03-17T09:12:06Z

kevin: quick checks — can someone paste the auth-proxy logs for the timeframe? also, are we seeing a cardinality spike? Grafana shows series count up 3x for the job.

marta: logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17T09:10:22Z] auth-proxy token validation failed: 401 invalid token, req_id=abc123 client_ip=10.4.72.19
[2026-03-17T09:10:22Z] auth-proxy token validation failed: 401 invalid token, req_id=abc124 client_ip=10.4.81.203
[2026-03-17T09:10:23Z] upstream error: 502 bad gateway -> token-service timeout
```

marta: also saw this in prometheus metrics: `prometheus_target_last_scrape_duration_seconds` for job="node-exporter" spiked and `prometheus_tsdb_head_samples_appended_total` slowed.

raj: digging into scrape labels — noticed the proxy started attaching `X-Request-Id` and `X-Client-Ip` as labels via relabeling in front of the proxy last week. that can explode cardinality if client_ip is left in.

alyssa: confirmed — relabel config on the proxy side has this snippet (oops):
```yaml
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__header_X-Client-Ip]
    target_label: client_ip
  - source_labels: [__header_X-Request-Id]
    target_label: request_id
```

kevin: yep that's the smoking gun. per-request request_id client_ip as labels = high-cardinality. that will also push remote_write throughput and cause backpressure/timeouts downstream.

sam: action plan? quick mitigation then proper patch.

raj: short-term: add a relabel rule to drop `client_ip` and `request_id` before they hit Prom:
```yaml
- action: labeldrop
  regex: "^(client_ip|request_id)$"
```
I'll push to the proxy config as a hotfix.

marta: also create a remote_write fallback to our west2-readonly endpoint to relieve the main ingest cluster while we fix auth token errors.

infra-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prometheus-high-cardinality — next step: labeldrop change, then watch series count and remote_write backlog.

kevin: while we patch, set the throttle on scrape manager to lower concurrent scrapes for that job: `--scrape-manager.max-concurrency=8` for the service. prevents pileup.

alyssa: patch submitted: `k8s deploy auth-proxy v2026.03.17-hotfix` with relabel labeldrop. rolling update started.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for deployment/auth-proxy (namespace=monitoring) — 6/6 pods updating

marta: after patch, series count dropped back toward baseline in the last 6m. remote_write backlog halved, p95 scrape latency down to ~450ms.

sam: nice. root cause: proxy relabeling client-scoped headers into metrics + token validation flakiness from token-service timeouts after nodepool IP changes.

raj: follow-ups: 1) remove all per-request IDs from relabeling config permanently 2) add e2e test for proxy to catch header->label regressions 3) make token-service healthchecks more resilient to nodepool IP churn (rotate allowed-audiences / add CIDR mapping)

kevin: opened ticket INFRA-7321 for the follow-ups and another INFRA-7322 to tighten alert thresholds for prometheus target cardinality. cc @marta @raj

sam: closing loop: hotfix reverted the relabeling and we rolled the token-service to a stable revision (no config change, just restart to pick up routing update). metrics normalized. will keep monitoring through the day. :thumbsup:
